the electromagnetic response of a spacecraft cavity to a dielectric discharge is not the same as the response of an unclattered cavity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

for a typical discharge in a cluttered cavity, the frequency response is not the same as that for an unclutterd cavity, and the frequency response is lower than expected from a simple calculation of the lowest mode.
a discharge across a narrow cavity gap can cause a response in the cavity which is not a simple superposition of the modes of the uncluttered structure.

the frequency response of an electromagnetic pulse in a cluttered cavity is lower than that of a simple coaxial cavity, and that it may be possible to predict the frequency response from knowledge of the geometry of the cavity.

the electromagnetic interference (EMI) signal caused by discharges within a spacecraft is much lower than the lowest mode of the uncluttered spacecraft cavity.
the frequency of the internal electromagnetic interference signal is much lower than expected for the lowest mode of the uncluttered DSCS II cavity.
